source.notes: 200,000 synthetic reads of 150bp spread evenly over 600,000bp, 50 rows deep, through alignments' own `computeLayout` on its plain path — no sort, no soft clips, no cap — against the same packing as the shared `stack` transform step. Five arms interleaved and rotated in one node 24 process, min of 11 rounds, on AC power with a load average under 1. The two implementations are checked row for row before any timing is believed and the run exits non-zero if they disagree, which is the point of the comparison: `stack` with `padding: 2` is `placeRect`'s clearance, so the rule is the same rule. 'layout' is today's call over the worker's `Uint32Array` of positions, answering a `Uint16Array` of rows; 'control' is the same call through a second driver literal, so `control / layout` is what this harness could resolve at all; 'stack' is the port — a `SimpleFeature` per read, `runTransforms` with one `stack` step, then the rows read back into the `Uint16Array` every pass downstream of the layout indexes by read; 'step' is that with the feature list already built and 'features' is building it, so the two split the port's cost into the step and the representation. A second run of the same command moved the absolute times ~10% and left every ratio within 0.05.
